intro: ^The golden sands of Egypt stretch endlessly before you. The year is 1923, and you've just arrived in Luxor as an aspiring archaeologist, following rumors of an undiscovered tomb near the Valley of the Kings.
^The locals speak in hushed tones of the Tomb of Khamenet, a forgotten pharaoh whose name was erased from history. They say his treasure remains cursed, guarded by ancient magic.
arrival: ^You arrive at the excavation site with your equipment: a leather satchel, rope, canteen, and your trusty journal. The desert sun beats down mercilessly as your guide, old Rashid, points to a narrow canyon.
^"There," he whispers. "The entrance was revealed by last week's sandstorm. But I will go no further. The old magic still lives."
^He leaves you alone. Before you lies a dark opening in the canyon wall, partially obscured by fallen rocks.
examine_entrance: ^You brush away sand and examine the entrance. Ancient hieroglyphs are carved around the doorway.

b: ^ You can read them: "Here lies Khamenet, Speaker of Truth. Only the worthy may enter."
^The symbols are mysterious, impossible to read without training.

examine_entrance: ^The entrance is large enough to crawl through. You notice torch brackets on the walls inside.
hasty_entrance: ^You hastily light a torch and duck into the passage. In your haste, you trip over loose stones, and your torch falls from your hand, rolling into the darkness ahead.
^Cursing, you're now in dim light. You can see the torch flickering ahead, but the passage seems unstable.
^Crawl forward carefully to retrieve the torch
retrieve_torch: ^You crawl forward slowly, testing each stone. Your caution pays off—you retrieve the torch just as a section of ceiling collapses behind you, sealing the entrance.
^There's no going back now. Only forward into the tomb.
careful_entrance: ^With torch held high, you enter the passage carefully. The walls are decorated with faded paintings showing the pharaoh's journey to the afterlife.
^As you move deeper, you hear a grinding sound behind you. Turning, you see stones settling into place, sealing the entrance.
^There's no retreat now. You must find another way out.
dark_entrance: ^You venture into the darkness, feeling your way along the walls. It's treacherous and frightening.
^After several minutes, you see a faint glow ahead. As you round a corner, you find yourself in a chamber lit by shafts of light from above.
search_area: ^You search the area around the entrance. Behind a large rock, you discover a small shrine with offerings left by ancient visitors. Among them is a bronze amulet with the Eye of Horus.
^You pocket the amulet. It might prove useful.

north_passage: ^As you step forward, the sphinx speaks with a voice like grinding stone:
^"I am the Guardian of Khamenet. Answer my riddle correctly, and pass. Answer incorrectly, and join the dust of centuries."
^"I never was, am always to be. No one ever saw me, nor ever will. And yet I am the confidence of all who live and breathe. What am I?"
riddle_correct: ^The sphinx's eyes dim to normal stone.
^"You are wise, seeker. You may pass—and return this way freely."
^A passage opens behind the sphinx, but you can also go back the way you came.
riddle_wrong: ^The chamber begins to shake. Sand pours from cracks in the ceiling. You run back the way you came, barely escaping as the passage collapses behind you.
^You're back in the first chamber, heart racing. The north passage is now blocked.
bypass_sphinx: ^You hold up the amulet. The sphinx's eyes widen in recognition.
^"You bear the mark of Khamenet himself! You are deemed worthy. Pass freely, seeker."
^The sphinx bows its great head, and a passage opens behind it.
east_passage: ^You enter the eastern passage. It slopes downward, leading to a small library chamber. Shelves carved into the walls hold dozens of ancient scrolls and papyri.

^The passages connect in a circle, with the burial chamber accessible from multiple routes. The safest path is through the east to the treasure chamber, then to the west where Khamenet lies.

^Your adventure ends here. The tomb keeps its secrets—and one more greedy soul.

west_passage: ^You enter the western passage. The walls here are painted with scenes of judgment in the afterlife—the weighing of the heart against the feather of Ma'at.
^The passage leads to an antechamber guarded by a priest's mummy, seated on a throne. Somehow, you sense it's not quite... dead.
^As you approach, the mummy's eyes open with a dusty creak.
^"Why do you disturb the rest of Khamenet?" it rasps.
^Say: "I wish to restore Khamenet's name to history"
^Say: "I mean no harm, only to document what's here"
priest_knowledge: ^"Knowledge is worthy. But what will you do with it?"
priest_restoration: ^The mummy sits forward eagerly, dust falling from its wrappings.
^"Yes! Khamenet was a good man, struck down by lies. If you would restore his name, you are a friend indeed."
priest_document: ^"A chronicler, then. That too has value. The truth should be recorded."
priest_amulet: ^You show the amulet. The priest gasps and bows his head.
^"You bear the mark! You are the one foretold—the one who would find the truth and speak it to the world. Enter freely, friend of Khamenet."

b: ^ The priest stands and bows. "You have proven yourself worthy. Enter the burial chamber. Learn the truth of Khamenet, and carry it to the world above." The passage behind him opens.
^ The priest nods. "You may pass, but remember: truth is sacred. Do not betray it." A passage opens behind him, though he watches you warily.

treasure_chamber: ^You find yourself in a central treasure chamber. Passages lead in multiple directions, and you can see how the tomb connects in a great circle.
^Here there are more treasures, but also something more valuable: detailed reliefs showing Khamenet's true history.
study_reliefs: ^The reliefs tell an amazing story. Khamenet discovered corruption among the priests and nobles. He tried to reform the system, to create fair laws and distribute food to the poor during a famine.
^For this, his rivals poisoned him and erased his name from history. But his loyal followers built this tomb in secret, preserving the truth.
burial_chamber: ^You enter the burial chamber. It's smaller than you expected, but beautiful. The sarcophagus is made of simple stone, not gold—Khamenet practiced the humility he preached.
^On the walls are his final words, written in his own hand:
^"To whoever finds this place: I was not perfect, but I tried to speak truth and serve justice. If you carry this truth forward, I will live again through your voice. That is immortality enough."

b: ^ The amulet glows warm against your chest.

burial_chamber: ^You realize you've found something more valuable than gold—a forgotten hero's true story.

find_exit: ^Behind the sarcophagus, you discover a hidden passage—an escape route carved by the loyal followers who built the tomb. It leads upward to the desert surface, emerging far from where you entered.
final_choice: ^As you climb toward the light, you must decide what to do with what you've found.
^Report the tomb, take credit and the gold
^Report the tomb, focus on Khamenet's story
^Seal the tomb and tell no one
ending_treasure: ^You emerge into the desert sunset, your pockets heavy with gold. You report the tomb to the authorities and lead an expedition back.

^The tomb is excavated, its treasures divided among museums. You become famous and wealthy. Yet sometimes, late at night, you wonder if you honored Khamenet's true wish—or if you became another grave robber with better credentials.
^Still, the story gets told, even if the gold gets more attention. Perhaps that's enough.
^'s adventure concludes. You found treasure and truth—though perhaps not in equal measure.
ending_knowledge: ^You emerge into the desert sunset, carrying only your notes, scrolls, and the truth of Khamenet's story.

^You spend years researching, translating, and writing. Your book about Khamenet becomes a landmark work, restoring his name to history. Museums add him to their pharaoh exhibitions. School children learn about the reformer king who died for justice.

b: ^ You donate the amulet to the Cairo Museum, where it's displayed as "The Seal of Khamenet."

ending_knowledge: ^You never became wealthy, but you gave a forgotten hero immortality. On quiet nights, you could swear you feel his gratitude.
^'s adventure concludes in triumph. You honored truth over gold, and the world is richer for it.
ending_secret: ^You emerge into the desert sunset and make a difficult choice: you seal the tomb's new entrance with rocks and tell no one.
^Some truths, you decide, are too precious to risk. In modern hands, Khamenet's tomb might become a circus—tourists posing with sarcophagi, treasures sold to private collectors.
^Let him rest in peace. You'll carry his story in your heart, living by the principles he died for. That's the real treasure.
^Years later, on your deathbed, you'll write down the location. Future generations can decide when the time is right.
^'s adventure concludes in silence. Sometimes the greatest discoveries are the ones we protect.
